- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean or 1–2 points.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp drop or volatility, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to account for mean reversion.
- After a model forecast spike (e.g., >+1.5% from prior), true outcome often corrects downward; cap next forecast at 1–2 points below peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.0), model often overpredicts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% or 1–2 points to avoid overconfidence.
- If true outcome deviates >3% from model in first 5–7 days, assume lag or misalignment; adjust forecast to align with recent 3–5 day true trend, not 30d trend.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows early volatility (e.g., first 5 days deviate >2%), reduce forecast slope or add 1–2 point downward correction to avoid overshoot.
